title: W-01: workflow:advance must not skip a phase
businessRules: W-01 is canonical in config/product-completeness.json only if a finding is added for it; this work item closes the demonstrated hole regardless. It closes only when workflow:advance rejects a skipped phase and a dependency-free test proves it; editing the phase string by hand to claim the fix is forbidden.

The defect was demonstrated, not hypothesised: while closing T360-20261014-131512 the advance commands were STAGING -> RELEASED -> CLOSED, because commandAdvance only rejects a phase whose order is lower than the current one. RELEASE_READY and its releaseEvidence check never ran, and the item file had to be backfilled after close.

A gate that can be bypassed by skipping the step that would have enforced it is not a gate. This is the same class as A-02 and must be closed by the same standard: the control derives the rule, the test proves the negative case, and nothing is weakened to make the happy path pass.

A transition is legal only when the target phase is the immediate successor of the current phase in config/workflow-policy.json phaseOrder. BLOCKED remains reachable from any phase and remains a dead end, matching the documented manual path for a blocked item.
RELEASE_READY must fail when releaseEvidence is empty; because every path to CLOSED now passes through RELEASE_READY, that check is reachable on every close and can no longer be skipped.
No existing assertion may be weakened, no phase may be removed from phaseOrder, and productReady, currentPhase and humanStage20 stay untouched.
acceptanceCriteria: workflow:advance rejects any non-BLOCKED transition whose target is not the immediate successor of the current phase, with an error naming both phases.
workflow:advance still allows a single-step advance through every phase, and still allows entering BLOCKED from any phase.

A dependency-free test proves the negative cases: a jump from STAGING to RELEASED is rejected; a jump from INTAKE to VERIFICATION is rejected; a step from STAGING to RELEASE_READY with empty releaseEvidence is rejected, and the same step succeeds once the evidence path is set.
The test also proves the positive case: a fresh item walks INTAKE through CLOSED one step at a time with no gaps.
Both GitHub heavy workflows and Workflow Governance stay green on the exact commit.
testPlan: node --test tests/workflow-phase-order.test.mjs — new control, negative and positive cases
npm run test:dependency-free — full suite, including workflow validation over the repository work items
npm run lint, npm run workflow:validate, npm run validate:repo, npm run audit:full:repo
GitHub exact-source Full Automated UAT and Full System Simulation — green with productionTouched false
migrationPlan: No schema migration. Only scripts/workflow.mjs and one dependency-free test change; no database object is added, altered or dropped.
rollbackPlan: Revert the commit. workflow:advance returns to allowing skips and the phase-order test disappears; nothing else changes and no data is written. The prior green commit remains a valid checkpoint.
monitoringPlan: The test runs inside test:dependency-free on every local run and on both heavy workflows, so a reintroduced skip fails the build rather than quietly bypassing RELEASE_READY.
securityNotes: Process integrity only. No secret, token, credential or personal data is read or written; no runtime path, permission or tenant check changes.
